chapter.title: Agent, chatbot, or plain script: picking the right tool

cards.body: You have 3 people in the office. A clerk who follows a checklist to the letter, never tires, never thinks. A friend you can ask anything, who answers and then goes back to their desk. And the new intern, who will go off and do a multi-step job for you, with judgement, and sometimes get it wrong. **Picking the right one for each task is the whole skill.**
cards.simpler: Picture three helpers in an office. One is a clerk who follows a checklist word for word. The clerk never gets tired and never thinks. One is a friend you can ask anything. They answer, then go back to their desk. The third is a new intern. They will go off and do a job with many steps, using their own judgement, and sometimes get it wrong. **Picking the right helper for each task is the whole skill.**

cards.prompt: Your photo folder has 500 files named IMG_0001 to IMG_0500. You want each renamed to the date it was taken. Who gets the job?

options.text: The intern, so they can use judgement on each photo
The clerk with a checklist: same exact steps, 500 times
The friend at the desk, who can tell you how renaming works

whyNot.a: That's handing judgement to a job that needs none: the path is identical for every file, so the intern just adds cost and risk.
whyNot.c: That's the chatbot: it can explain the steps, but it stops after answering. Nothing gets renamed.

cards.reteach: When every step is known before you start, you want a script: ordinary code that does the same thing every time. There is nothing to decide, so there is nothing for a model to think about.

cards.title: Question 1: is the path known in advance?
cards.body:
Before you reach for an agent, ask one question first. **Could you write down every step before starting?** If yes, that is a *script*: plain code that runs the same steps every time. Renaming files, resizing photos, copying rows from one sheet to another. A script is cheaper, faster, and never invents anything.

If the steps depend on what you find along the way, a script cannot do it. 'Find out which of these 3 laptops is best for me' has no fixed path. You read one review, that changes what you search next. That is where thinking in the loop earns its keep.
cards.simpler: Before you use an agent, ask one thing. **Could you write down every step before you start?** If yes, use a script. A script is plain code that runs the same steps every time, like a recipe. It is cheaper, faster, and never makes things up. If each step depends on what you found before, a script cannot help. Picking the best of three laptops has no fixed path. One review changes your next search. That needs an agent.

cards.title: The 500 files, done 3 ways
cards.body: Priya has 500 photos to rename. She tries the chatbot first. It writes her a perfect 6-line script and wishes her luck. She tries an agent next. It renames 490 files correctly, gets confused by 10 with missing dates, and quietly names them all 'unknown'. Then she runs the chatbot's script. 500 files, 2 seconds, and the 10 with missing dates stop with an error so she can see them. The clerk wins. The agent took 4 minutes and hid the problem.
cards.simpler: Priya has 500 photos to rename. She asks the chatbot first. It writes a short script for her and wishes her luck. Next she tries an agent. It renames 490 files right, gets confused by 10 with missing dates, and quietly calls them all 'unknown'. Then she runs the chatbot's script. 500 files, 2 seconds. The 10 with missing dates stop with an error so she can see them. **The clerk wins.** The agent took 4 minutes and hid the problem.

cards.prompt: Your inbox has 300 unread emails. You want them sorted into 'needs reply', 'read later', and 'ignore'. The rules are fuzzy: it depends who sent it and what it asks. What fits?

options.text: A script, since sorting email is a known task
An agent, since each email needs a judgement call and the mistake cost is low
A chatbot, since you can paste each email in and ask

whyNot.a: That's the clerk on a job with no checklist: 'depends who sent it' means the path is not known in advance, so plain code cannot do it.
whyNot.c: That's the friend at the desk, 300 times. It can judge one email, but it will not go through the inbox for you.

cards.reteach: Ask the 3 questions. Path known? No, each email is different. Mistake bad? No, a mislabelled email is easy to fix. Needs judgement at each step? Yes. All 3 point to the intern: an agent.

cards.title: Questions 2 and 3: how bad is a mistake, and does it need judgement?
cards.body:
**Question 2: how bad is one mistake?** A mislabelled email costs you 10 seconds. A wrongly sent payment costs you a week. The worse the mistake, the more you want a script you can test, or an agent with a human 'yes' before the risky step.

**Question 3: does it need judgement at each step?** If the answer is 'no, just once, then I'll act', that is a chatbot. 'Which laptop should I buy?' is a chatbot question. 'Research 3 laptops, compare prices today, and put a table in my notes' is an agent task. Same topic, different tool, because the second one keeps going without you.
cards.simpler: Two more questions. **How bad is one mistake, and does it need judgement at each step?** A mislabelled email costs seconds. A wrong payment costs a week. The worse the mistake, the more you want a tested script, or an agent that asks you first. One answer and then you act is a chatbot, like asking which laptop to buy. 'Research 3 laptops and put the prices in my notes' is an agent task. It keeps going without you.

cards.body: Marcus is excited about agents, so he builds one to back up his work folder every night. It works for 3 weeks. Then one night the model decides a half-finished file 'looks like junk' and skips it. Nobody notices for a month. The tell: he gave judgement to a job that needed none. **If you could have written the steps on a sticky note, use a script.**
cards.simpler: Marcus loves agents, so he builds one to back up his work folder every night. It runs fine for 3 weeks. Then one night the model decides a half-finished file looks like junk and skips it. Nobody notices for a month. The warning sign: he gave judgement to a job that needed none. A backup should copy everything, no opinions. **If you could have written the steps on a sticky note, use a script.**

cards.prompt: Dana wants to know whether a used car listing is a good deal. She has the listing open and will decide herself. Which tool?

options.text: A chatbot: one question, one answer, then she acts
An agent, because it involves money
A script, because checking a price is a fixed step

whyNot.b: That's the agent's cue, but only when the task has many steps and she is not in the loop. Here she decides herself after one answer. Money alone does not call for an intern.
whyNot.c: That's the clerk's cue, but 'is this a good deal' has no fixed checklist. It needs judgement, just once.

cards.reteach: The chatbot fits when you need one judgement and then you take over. An agent fits when the judgement has to happen again and again across steps you are not watching. Dana is watching, so one answer is enough.

cards.title: In one breath
cards.body: **Three questions pick the tool:** is the path known, how bad is a mistake, does it need judgement at each step. Known path means script, one judgement means chatbot, many judgements across steps you won't watch means agent, and the worse the mistake, the more you want a human click before the risky step.
cards.simpler: **Three questions pick the tool.** Is the path known? How bad is a mistake? Does it need judgement at each step? A known path means a script. One judgement means a chatbot. Many judgements across steps you will not watch means an agent. And the worse a mistake would be, the more you want a human to click 'yes' before the risky step.

cards.body: Write down 3 chores from your week. Next to each, put S, C or A for script, chatbot or agent, and one word for why. Keep the note. Day 14 will revisit it.
cards.simpler: **Write down 3 chores from your week.** Next to each one, put S, C or A. S is script, C is chatbot, A is agent. Add one word for why you chose it. Keep the note somewhere you will find it again. Day 14 will revisit it.

chapter.outcomeLine: You can now take 3 tasks from your own week, run each through the 3-question test, and say which deserves an agent, which a chatbot, and which a plain script, with the reason.
